title: Office.com website, 2013
lede: A red-orange Office 365 panel and light Segoe headings on a white page with blue link lists.
summary: Solid red-orange hero panel with a light white headline and a flat green button, over three columns of light headings. April 2013.

evidence.note: Captured with `tools/capture.mjs` (headless Chrome, 1440 × 900) on 28 September 2026 from the Wayback Machine copy of 1 April 2013, and inspected. The screenshot shows the first viewport; the measurement covers up to four screens. Nothing covers the page. The headings render in a light Segoe-like face.

styles.note: Clear: a solid red-orange panel with a flat green button and light headings; the rest is white space, light headings, and blue text links.

observed: A dark gray top bar holds the white Office logo. Below it, uppercase navigation has the active item in red-orange.
The search field is a thin gray outline with a red-orange magnifier glyph.

A solid red-orange panel holds the Office 365 logo, the headline “Transform how you run your business with Office 365” in large light white type, and a square green “Try it for free” button. A photograph fills its right half.
Three columns have large light headings: “What’s New in Office?”, “Get Templates”, and “Office for Home Use”. Each has a picture and a list of blue text links.
A pale gray band at the bottom holds more headings.
interpretation: Measured: headings weight 400 in Segoe UI and Segoe UI Light; 16% of screenshot pixels are saturated; no shadows or gradients. 33% of boxes have a 1 px border, from the search field and hairline dividers on a page with only 9 filled boxes.
borrow: Put one saturated panel at the top of an otherwise white page, and set its headline in a light weight at large size.

images.alt: Office.com home page of April 2013: a dark top bar, a search field, a red-orange Office 365 panel with a light white headline and green Try it for free button next to a photo of a man at a laptop, and three columns with light headings and blue links.
images.caption: First viewport of the [Wayback Machine copy of office.microsoft.com, 1 April 2013](https://web.archive.org/web/20130401081631/http://office.microsoft.com/en-us/).
